claim: The captured PubMed abstract for Fong and Ratwani reports that their three-phase framework was applied to 457 interruption episodes captured during 36 hours of observation. It reports immediate suspension of the interrupted task in 348/457 episodes (76.1%), new self-initiated tasks during the interrupting task in 164/457 (35.9%), and no direct resumption of the interrupted task in 284/457 (62.1%). These are descriptive observations for the reported episodes, not generic rates or transition probabilities. The abstract does not state physician count, site count, calendar observation period, episode inclusion details, or coding definitions for suspension and nested work. It provides no eligible-task/choice-set snapshots, first-subsequent-task result, eventual-resumption outcome, or resumption latency; those fields remain unknown. No policy, model default, distribution, or fitted parameter is assigned.
